text.p: The following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A new $30 million complex to rehabilitate up to 300 juvenile delinquent boys will open at Jurong Road in November next year.
- Thousands of South Korean workers, angered by the arrests of three militant union leaders, marched on Seoul's Myongdong Cathedral where seven strike leaders have taken shelter.
- Singaporeans splurged more than $1 billion on Mercedes-Benz cars last year and their favourite was the new E-class.

- PrOperty magnate Ng Teng Fong has put in a higher than expected top bids for two condominium sites in the latest state tender in what is seen as a move to shore up sluggish prices fetched at previous auctions.

- At least 10 foreign telecommunications companies have been courting Singapore firms in preparation for the upcoming basic telecommunications licences, but only a handful are expected to hand in their bids later this year.

- Creative Technlogy has revamped the way it handles its major non-audio products, underlining the company's growing confidence in a strategy that recently caused jitters but is now winning influential support.
- Tycoon Ng Teng Fong, who has been relatively quiet in land buying recently, emerged as top bidder for the two more popular of four Housing and Development Board (HDB) sites.
- Indonesian companies, hoping to raise money in a booming stock market, are facing waning foreign investor enthusiasm due to the coming parliamentary elections in May.
